rows.why: S1 covers the BOM, header, row order and CRLF, which items 1, 2, 4 and 5 each address. Item 1 (columns, order and header names) is closest to the scenario's core, 'the header and one row per requisition'. Its run starts with U+FEFF, has the header 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created', and ends every row, the last included, with CRLF. Item 2's sort (creation time, then id) also matches.

No item asks how status is displayed. Item 9 asks how the creation time is formatted, which S2 settles as a UTC 'YYYY-MM-DD' date. The run writes the full ISO string '2023-11-14T22:13:20.123Z', not just the date. The runs also show status written as lowercase 'open' rather than 'Open'. Item 8 (empty field for a missing title) agrees, but it covers only a minor part of S2.
Item 3 asks what an empty list produces. The run returns only the BOM and the header row followed by CRLF, which is what S3 expects.

Item 6 asks how fields with commas, quotes or line breaks are escaped. The run wraps such a field in quotes and doubles the inner quotes, as S4 requires. But S4 also requires quoting a title that starts or ends with a space. RFC 4180 does not require that, and nothing was run for it, so agreement on that part can't be determined.
Item 7 asks how formula-like leading characters are handled. The run writes '=SUM(A1)' and '@x' unchanged, but S5 requires a single quote in front.

Item 10 asks what happens with bad row data: unknown status, invalid counts, filled greater than openings, or an invalid date. The run throws 'Requisition bad7 has more filled than openings', which names the requisition id as S6 requires.
